entries.summary: Fixed strict cloud-sdk MetaData.parseJson bug: parse SQS body leniently via booking.util.MetaData then bridge to cloud-sdk MetaData.Builder in all 3 tasks. Task test green.
entries.detail: Bug found+fixed via tests: cloud-sdk MetaData.parseJson is STRICT (rejects unknown fields) and threw UnrecognizedPropertyException on real SQS bodies which carry extra wire fields (notificationParties, externalIdentifiers). Fix: in all 3 tasks (WatermillBKTask, WatermillBKAperakTask, CargoVisibilitySubscriptionPublisherTask.parseMetaData) parse the body LENIENTLY via Json.fromJsonString(payload, com.inttra.mercury.booking.util.MetaData.class) (watermill Json has FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN=false) then bridge to cloud-sdk MetaData via new MetaData.Builder(workflowId,parentWorkflowId,rootWorkflowId,bucket,fileName,component,timestamp).setExitStatus/.setMessageId/.setProjections(nonNull).build(). This keeps backward-compat with existing producers. WatermillBKTaskTest 4/4 green after fix. watermill-booking full suite prior: 259 tests, only WatermillBKTaskTest failed (now fixed).

entries.summary: cloud-sdk gap: DynamoDbAdminCommand ignores @DynamoDbAttribute on partition key (uses property name hashKey not id). Zero live impact (idempotent skip; table pre-exists as id). Documented + IT asserts structurally.
entries.detail: cloud-sdk GAP found during cargo-viz DynamoDB migration: DynamoDbAdminCommand derives the partition-key ATTRIBUTE name from the bean PROPERTY name (hashKey), ignoring @DynamoDbAttribute("id"). So a FRESH table gets hash key attribute "hashKey" while the enhanced-client DAO (BeanTableSchema) correctly uses "id" (CargoVisibilitySubscriptionDaoIT passes with id). GSIs are unaffected (their properties carrierBookingNumber/billOfLadingNumber/subscriptionReference/carrierIntttraId match live attribute names, no rename). Impact: ZERO in all live envs (INT/QA/CVT/PROD) because the table already exists with "id" (legacy command) and the new admin command is idempotent -> skips. Only a brand-new env would get the wrong partition-key attribute. Chose NOT to rename entity property hashKey->id (75 usages across task/TransformationHelper/DAO/tests/JSON resources + divergence from visibility which ships hashKey+@DynamoDbAttribute and never provisions this table via admin command). Proposed cloud-sdk enhancement: DynamoDbAdminCommand should derive the partition/sort key attribute names from BeanTableSchema (respecting @DynamoDbAttribute), not the bean property name. CargoVisibilitySubscriptionTableCommandIT.createsTable asserts single HASH key structurally (not the attribute name) with an explanatory comment; createsThreeGsis + idempotency assertions unchanged.

entries.summary: Decision on ApproximateReceiveCount cloud-sdk gap: preserve functional behavior by requesting the system attribute via minimal AWS SDK v2 SqsClient in the listener (cloud-sdk kept for send/delete). Adapt RetryClassifier/RetryableOperation v1->v2 exceptions.
entries.detail:
HARD CONFLICT: develop ION-16235 retry feature reads SQS ApproximateReceiveCount via message.getAttributes() for (1) WARN->ERROR escalation at attempt>=3 and (2) isUnacknowledgedRedelivery -> republish a subscription persisted in DynamoDB but crashed before Watermill publish. Decompiled cloud-sdk SqsMessagingClient in BOTH 1.0.17-SNAPSHOT and 1.0.28-SNAPSHOT: receiveMessages(ReceiveMessageOptions) builds ReceiveMessageRequest with only queueUrl/maxNumberOfMessages/waitTimeSeconds; it NEVER calls messageSystemAttributeNames/attributeNames, and MessagingClient/AwsMessagingClientConfig/MessagingClientFactory expose NO way to request system attributes. So QueueMessage.getAttributes() will NOT contain ApproximateReceiveCount at runtime -> republish safety-net would silently no-op.
DECISION (autonomous, user unavailable): PRESERVE full functional behavior (functional-priority directive). Keep cloud-sdk MessagingClient for send/delete/queueAttributes. For the LISTENER receive path in watermill-commons SQSListenerClient, use a minimal AWS SDK v2 SqsClient receive that requests messageSystemAttributeNames(APPROXIMATE_RECEIVE_COUNT) and adapt results to cloud-sdk QueueMessage<String>. This stays on AWS SDK 2.x (the migration's actual target), preserves runtime functionality, and keeps all unit tests (which mock QueueMessage.getAttributes) passing. Will document as the cloud-sdk ApproximateReceiveCount gap + resolution. Also must adapt RetryClassifier/RetryableOperation from AWS SDK v1 exception types (com.amazonaws.*, v1 ProvisionedThroughputExceededException) to AWS SDK v2 (software.amazon.awssdk.*).

entries.summary: Added doc §9: minimal cloud-sdk 1.0.28 enhancement to request SQS system attributes on receive (wire messageSystemAttributeNames into ReceiveMessageOptions/SqsMessagingClient) so watermill can drop the direct AWS v2 SqsClient; response side (SqsMessage.getAttributes) already handles it.
entries.detail: Confirmed the AWS-v2 SqsClient ApproximateReceiveCount workaround works (INT boot SQSListener polls; SqsQueueMessageTest/SQSListenerClientTest pass). Reviewed cloud-sdk 1.0.28-SNAPSHOT and added doc section 9 'Proposed cloud-sdk enhancement'. Key 1.0.28 finding: SqsMessagingClient.receiveMessages(ReceiveMessageOptions) builds ReceiveMessageRequest with only queueUrl/maxNumberOfMessages/waitTimeSeconds and DROPS ReceiveMessageOptions.getAttributes() + getVisibilityTimeoutSeconds(); it never calls messageSystemAttributeNames. But SqsMessage.getAttributes() ALREADY copies all present system attributes -> response side fine. Minimal fix: add messageSystemAttributeNames (List<String>) to ReceiveMessageOptions (cloud-sdk-api) and wire .messageSystemAttributeNamesWithStrings(...) (+ visibilityTimeout) in SqsMessagingClient.receiveMessages (cloud-sdk-aws); optional default-request ApproximateReceiveCount. Additive/backward-compatible. Doc lists exact watermill files to revert (SQSListenerClient->MessagingClient, delete SqsQueueMessage+test, 3 injectors + tests) once SDK ships. Suggested raising a mercury-services-commons ticket for next SNAPSHOT after 1.0.28. Doc is git-ignored (on-disk reference).
